idiom_name: sealed record node hierarchy + a Children property
implementation_notes: C# realizes the pattern with an abstract record Node that declares the normalized child accessor (public abstract IReadOnlyList<Node> Children { get; }) and one sealed record per node kind holding its node-specific data in positional properties; generic passes recurse over Children, and per-node dispatch is a switch expression with type and property patterns. The compiler-synthesized record members replace the classic constructor/equality boilerplate, but C# does not prove exhaustiveness of a switch, so keep a default arm that throws. Roslyn uses the same shape at scale: every syntax node is a distinct class and ChildNodes() (verified) plus DescendantNodes() walk any node uniformly.
pitfalls: Record equality and GetHashCode recurse through the whole tree: comparing or hashing two large trees is O(tree) and can overflow the stack - use reference semantics or override equality when nodes denote tree nodes rather than values.
Children as a computed property allocates a fresh array per access; cache it in the record or expose an explicit iterator for hot passes.
Pattern switches over records are not proved exhaustive by the compiler: a newly added node type silently reaches the default arm unless it throws.
